name: 紅頂綠鳩
illustrationTaxon: Treron formosae formosae adult male (Taiwan population); distinct from split Ryukyu Green Pigeon Treron permagnus

similarSpecies.distinction: 紅翅綠鳩有顯著白腹、腿周白羽和較寬的白色尾下羽緣；紅頂綠鳩台灣亞種雄鳥有橙金冠及紫褐肩斑，腹部偏綠黃且沒有白色腿羽。
楔尾綠鳩有銅金冠胸、栗色肩羽與寬基楔形尾；紅頂綠鳩台灣雄鳥較小、冠橙紅、肩斑紫褐，尾較短。

featureNotes: 指名亞種雄鳥冠呈深金橙色，雌鳥較黯淡且沒有金冠
雄鳥內側翼覆羽與肩羽呈紫褐色；雌鳥缺此肩斑
羽腿為綠色而非白色，足紅；與紅翅綠鳩的白腿羽區別
尾下覆羽有窄白緣、中央深色縱紋；較紅翅綠鳩白緣窄

rangeMap.note: Current Treron formosae sensu stricto occurs natively in Taiwan and the Batanes/Babuyan islands of the northern Philippines. Highlights indicate broad geographic context only, not nationwide occupancy or exact range polygons. The single Hong Kong record formerly grouped within Whistling Green-Pigeon is now treated by HKBWS as the separate Ryukyu Green Pigeon Treron permagnus, not as a confirmed occurrence of current T. formosae.

sources.use: BirdLife/IUCN current Taiwan Green-pigeon Treron formosae account read: Near Threatened (2023), population 1,250–2,000 mature individuals, trend decreasing; current range is Taiwan and northern Philippine islands (Batan, Calayan, Camiguin Norte, Sabtang).

Cornell eBird/Merlin Whistling Green-Pigeon account read under the broader pre-split taxon concept: lowland broadleaf evergreen forest; Taiwan and Ryukyu forms are sometimes treated separately; Taiwan birds are smaller and have a rufous cap; compared with White-bellied Green-Pigeon, no white feathering around legs, less yellow face and narrower white edges on undertail coverts.

Current HKBWS account read: this profile is Ryukyu Green Pigeon Treron permagnus, Category I accidental; the sole HK record was photographed on Po Toi on 14 Nov 2012, subspecies uncertain. HKBWS describes a close resemblance to White-bellied Green Pigeon but no contrasting white belly, broad dark centres and narrow pale fringes on longer undertail coverts. Used only to document the taxonomic reassignment/local record; not as evidence that current T. formosae occurs in HK.

The current HKBWS Hong Kong occurrence is classified as T. permagnus, which was split from the older T. formosae/Whistling Green-Pigeon complex; it is not presented as a confirmed HK record of runtime T. formosae.
Current global IUCN status for T. formosae is Near Threatened; do not use the older LC status attached to the former broad complex or current T. permagnus.
